supersedes.scope: Selection color mapping only. R200 remains valid evidence for the SR10.4 label-selection geometry and the standard GtkIconView full-cell fill.

rule: Every adapted state uses the active KDE semantic roles. Historical RGB is comparison evidence, not permission to hard-code or synthesize a final color.

implementation.refresh: Values are re-read from the active exported KDE palette whenever the GTK2 palette bridge rebuilds the RC.

native_previews.runtime: Native GtkIconView in private Xvfb, one focused selected item, GTK 2.24.33, 1:1 pixels.

scope_limit: Each preview substitutes that scheme's actual View and Selection role pairs into the private GTK2 fixture. Other role families remain at the DomainOS baseline; these are selection-color consumer checks, not whole-theme previews. No global KDE scheme was changed.

automated_validation.coverage: GTK2 role mapping and live palette refresh; related Motif geometry/asset regression checks.

result: The GTK2 selection now follows KDE Selection face and text roles across DomainOS, Breeze Light, Cybermil dark, and Steamed yellow-accent palettes. This restores schema consistency and supersedes R200's contrast-derived black/white pair. It intentionally no longer claims the VUE historical selection hue. The full-cell selection geometry remains different from VUE's label-only reverse video, as established in R200.
limits: No live GTK2 application or XChat process was changed or restarted.
The screenshots validate the selected-color consumer using actual View/Selection roles; they do not represent full palette exports for all non-selection controls.
Hover, rubberband and selection-fill geometry remain open; the GtkIconView fill is painted over the complete item rectangle by GTK2 upstream code.
next: Keep I167 open and GTK2 as the sole active family. Continue with the next GTK2 state/control that can be compared without changing another work-board section or applying the incomplete theme to XChat.
